sources.name: Medical-Surgical Nursing: Oncological Disorders
sources.text: A lymphoma applies to any cancer that begins in the lymphatic system. A leukemia refers to cancers of the blood-forming tissues, such as bone marrow. Blood cancers include leukemia , lymphoma , and myeloma. Leukemia is the profuse development of abnormal and immature white blood cells that are so numerous that they crowd out healthy cells. Lymphoma affects the lymphatic system, which changes how the lymph system functions as part of the immune system. Myeloma is a cancer that affects plasma cells, which are a type of white blood cell. Lymphoma Lymphoma develops in the lymphatic system. Lymphomas are associated with certain infections, such as Epstein-Barr virus, HIV, certain strains of herpes virus, and hepatitis C seropositivity.
